observations: Front view of a black Nikon mirrorless camera body.
The brand 'Nikon' is visible on the viewfinder housing in photo 0.
A 'Z' logo is visible on the camera's right shoulder in photo 0.
The lens mount is open, exposing the image sensor.
No lens or body cap is attached.

claims.evidence: The 'Nikon' and 'Z' branding are visible in photo 0, but the specific '8' model designation is not legible.
The Nikon Z series is a professional-grade mirrorless system.
The sensor size visible in the mount in photo 0 is consistent with a full-frame sensor.

risks.risk: The specific model (Z8 vs Z6/Z7) significantly changes the value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model name badge, usually located on the top or front corner.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a base Nikon Z5 model.

risks.risk: The sensor is exposed and may be scratched or heavily soiled.
risks.proof: A high-resolution close-up photo of the sensor surface under bright light.
risks.if_unproven: priced as requiring a professional sensor replacement.

risks.risk: The camera may not power on or have functional defects.
risks.proof: A photo or video of the rear LCD screen powered on and showing the menu.

risks.risk: High shutter count indicating heavy professional use.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the last image's metadata showing the total shutter actuations.
risks.if_unproven: priced as high mileage/near end of life.

proof_requests: Photo of the model name (Z8) clearly visible on the camera body.
Photo of the rear LCD screen powered on.
Close-up photo of the image sensor to check for scratches.
Screenshot of the current shutter count from the metadata.
response.reason: The specific model number '8' cannot be read in the photo, and the price difference between Nikon Z models is too large to estimate without confirmation. Furthermore, the sensor is exposed and there is no proof the device powers on.
